content.text: Hello! Today, we will learn about **Top View**, **Right View**, and the **Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA)** of a Binary Tree. These are very popular interview questions that test your understanding of tree geometry and traversals. Let's explore them!

· **Top View**: Imagine standing directly above a tree looking down. You will only see the nodes that are at the outermost boundaries of each column. We can compute this using Level Order traversal and column indexes (vertical distance from root).
· **Right View**: Imagine standing to the right of a tree. You will only see the rightmost node at each vertical level. We can compute this using a modified Preorder traversal (Root → Right → Left).
The **Lowest Common Ancestor** of two nodes $p$ and $q$ is the lowest node in the tree that has both $p$ and $q$ as descendants (where we allow a node to be a descendant of itself).
· **Real-World Analogy**: Think of it like finding the closest common manager in a company chart for two employees. It is the first manager going upwards who has authority over both.

content.text: Let's summarize: Tree views isolate specific perspectives: Top View uses columns, while Right View captures the last node at each level. The Lowest Common Ancestor is the deepest node where paths to $p$ and $q$ split. Next, we will introduce Binary Search Trees (BST)!
